summary: USB-C PD negotiation fails after BIOS/EC update causing reduced power state and blocked provisioning tasks
description: Issue summary: After the 2026-03 BIOS/EC bundle (BIOS v1.20 / EC v2.4.1) rolled out to a subset of docked laptops, affected devices fail to complete USB-C Power Delivery (PD) negotiation with company docks and third-party 65W/90W chargers. Impact: devices boot but remain in a reduced performance/power mode (S0ix-like behavior) which prevents provisioning sequences (SCCM task sequence, Intune device configuration, BitLocker key escrow) from completing. Several depot repairs reported devices not charging while showing 'AC connected' in OS. Environment: production depot imaging fleet and end-user docking stations in US office clusters.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Take a device with BIOS v1.20 / EC v2.4.1 installed.
2) Connect to a corporate USB-C dock or a 65W PD charger.
3) Observe Windows power state and the power_partner negotiation logs in EC.
4) Initiate an SCCM task sequence imaging or reboot into OOBE.
5) Provisioning stalls at 'Applying device configuration' and BitLocker escrow step times out.
6) Disconnect and reconnect charger; device may show 'Charging' but remains at reduced clock frequencies.
logs:
[EC][PD] PD_NEGOTIATE: requested 90W -> partner rejected; fallback to PD contract 7W
[OS][Power] AC_PRESENT=1 BATTERY_CHARGING=0 AC_ADAPTER=PD_UNKNOWN
[SCCM] TaskSequenceEngine: Waiting for network; NIC up but uefi_sysfs reports power-limited
[Intune] DeviceCompliance: SCEP enrollment attempt timed out after 00:05:12
[Diag] EC_FW: v2.4.1 build 20260302 CHECKSUM_OK=1 but PD_STATE=ERR_NEGOTIATION
comments: Marisol Vega (Tech): First reported from depot techs on 2026-03-09 after BIOS pushed overnight. Multiple units in bench fail provisioning. Captured EC and PD logs attached to ticket.
Devon Hart (Endpoint Eng): Reproduced locally on an X1 with dock T1. EC log shows PD handshake abort when PD contract higher than 15W. Suspect EC PD policy change in v2.4.1.

SRE (A. Kim): We saw a small bump in provisioning failures in monitoring starting 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC coincident with staged BIOS rollout. Rolling back one device to BIOS v1.19/EC v2.3.8 restored normal PD negotiation and provisioning completed.
Depot Lead (K. O'Neil): Two repaired units returned to customers re-flashed to EC v2.3.8 and passed SCCM imaging. Holding back further BIOS rollouts pending vendor response.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: EC v2.4.1 introduced a more restrictive PD sink policy that rejects certain PD source descriptors (particularly on legacy third-party chargers and older corporate docks). The OS sees AC present but power delivery limited, which causes the firmware to throttle CPU and prevents timeout-sensitive provisioning steps from completing. Evidence: rollback devices succeed; captured PD frames show 'CapabilityMismatch' and immediate RST from EC. Initial vendor triage indicates a changed PD negotiation timeout and stricter PD class enforcement. Affected models share same EC family (EC-Apollo) with identical PD policy code path.
resolution: Short-term workaround: 1) For depot imaging and urgent reimaging, re-flash EC to v2.3.8 and hold BIOS at v1.19 for impacted serial ranges. 2) Update SCCM task sequence to allow provisioning to continue on battery/limited PD for devices marked with label 'allow-provision-on-low-power' (temporary task sequence branch). 3) Advise field techs to use vetted 65W/90W certified PD supplies from our parts inventory (PN: PD-90C-RW) instead of user-supplied chargers. Long-term: Vendor to provide EC v2.4.2 with PD negotiation timeout revert or a compatibility flag. RFC open to block automatic BIOS/EC rollout until vendor patch and QA approval. Rollout notes: plan staggered redeploy with telemetry gating and a preflight script to validate PD negotiation before marking device healthy.
